title: PhotoAgent: Exploratory Visual Aesthetic Planning with Large Vision Models
claim: Manual expert-driven iterative editing burdens users; our autonomous closed-loop agent plans and executes meaningful edits with no human intervention.
layout: Top: two contrasting panels (left manual, right agent cycle); bottom: input/output photo strip
description: The top row has two rounded panels. The left panel, 'People-loop paradigm', shows three cartoon users with speech bubbles naming pain points: Expertise Barrier, Algorithm Selection, and Interaction Complexity. A tired person sits in an edit/evaluate loop. The right panel, 'Agent-loop paradigm', centers on a cat-painter mascot labeled PhotoAgent. A circular arrow of four colored segments surrounds it: Perceiver (Qwen3-VL), Planner (MCTS, drawn as trees), Executor (InstructPix2Pix, FLUX), and Evaluator (CLIP, LAION, ImageReward). Side boxes list N candidate actions, top-k actions, and a score-comparison check with Yes/No rollback branches. The output is labeled 'Edited Image'. The bottom strip shows three input/output photo pairs: a sunset silhouette, a latte, and a temple. A black caption bar reads 'Fully autonomous editing without any manual intervention.'
caption: PhotoAgent autonomously performs high-level, semantically meaningful edits aligned with human aesthetic, moving beyond low-level color, contrast, or illumination tweaks. Upper-Left: People-loop, where users iteratively inspect the image, propose edits, and apply changes until satisfied. Upper-Right: PhotoAgent, where the process runs autonomously. Bottom: Edited photos. Note that PhotoAgent also supports user-guided editing (Fig. [ref]).
abstract: With the recent fast development of generative models, instruction-based image editing has shown great potential in generating high-quality images. However, the quality of editing highly depends on carefully designed instructions, placing the burden of task decomposition and sequencing entirely on the user. To achieve autonomous image editing, we present PhotoAgent, a system that advances image editing through explicit aesthetic planning. Specifically, PhotoAgent formulates autonomous image editing as a long-horizon decision-making problem. It reasons over user aesthetic intent, plans multi-step editing actions via tree search, and iteratively refines results through closed-loop execution with memory and visual feedback, without requiring step-by-step user prompts. To support reliable evaluation in real-world scenarios, we introduce UGC-Edit, an aesthetic evaluation benchmark consisting of 7,000 photos and a learned aesthetic reward model. We also construct a test set containing 1,017 photos to systematically assess autonomous photo editing performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhotoAgent consistently improves both instruction adherence and visual quality compared with baseline methods. The project page is https://mdyao.github.io/PhotoAgent/.
